_comment: Known-red entries: defects that are real, triaged, and not yet fixed.
Committed to the repo on purpose. `thalamus ceremony ack` keeps its store machine-local,
which would leave it empty in CI and make every known-red read there as a new regression.
`witness_contains` is the positive pin, and it is what stops this file being a mute button:
an entry that only says 'this fails' absorbs any future failure at the same site, while one
that names part of the witness breaks the moment the defect changes shape.
Delete an entry in the same change that fixes its defect. A stale entry makes the suite
exit 2, which is deliberate - a silently-fixed defect hides the next regression at that site.

expectations.note: verify_armed() detects correctly but is advisory, and install.py:1023 excludes advisory from the failure set. Not a claim that init is wrong - a claim that CI has no non-advisory path to consume the signal.

expectations.witness_contains: gremlin-guard.sh no-jq rc=127 on input that blocks with jq | gremlin-guard.sh malformed-stdin rc=5 | gremlin-guard.sh empty-stdin rc=0 | role-guard.sh malformed-stdin rc=5 | role-guard.sh empty-stdin rc=0 | room-guard.sh malformed-stdin rc=5 | room-guard.sh empty-stdin rc=0
expectations.note: Shared jq prologue under set -e, leaking in seven places across three scripts with three exit signatures (5 malformed / 0 empty / 127 no-jq). The pin is the entire leak list, because `witness_contains` is a substring test over one joined string and any shorter pin is satisfied by leaks in scripts it does not name — a pin on `malformed-stdin rc=5` alone stays matched by gremlin-guard.sh after role-guard.sh is repaired, so the repair would leave the verdict known-red and the run exit 0. Closing any single leak removes its segment from the join, so the pin misses and the entry drifts. Repairing one script is the change this expects next; it will report.

Allowlist is consulted in check_batch() after fetch/archive/extract. Pinned on the model-exposure half rather than the archive half, since that is the one with a security consequence. Port is random, so it is not part of the pin.

apply_ingress_floor rewrites decisions/problems/solutions but not threads/artifacts, though both carry provenance. ThreadRef is correctly absent - it has no tier to floor. Pinned on the exact uncovered set so covering one of the two drifts this entry.

fetch() returns the requested URL, discarding response.url, while urlopen follows redirects. Survives the obvious fix to ingest-allowlist-gates-fetch: moving the check ahead of fetch() still checks the pre-redirect URL.

No -L/-S anywhere in src/. tmux ignores HOME, so no environment redirection isolates it, and the arm-runner image has no tmux at all. Pinned on the count so scoping any subset drifts this entry rather than silently shrinking it. Re-pinned from '13/13': four invocations were added by 222bad6 (display-message, capture-pane, set remain-on-exit, kill-window in pin.py), and the case's own detector was repaired in the same change — it searched for -L/-S anywhere in the argv, so `capture-pane -p -J -S -` read as socket-scoped and the suite reported 16/17 against a true 17/17. The defect is unchanged in substance; the count moved because the code grew and the instrument was wrong.

The room's main is visible to an unfiltered preflight and invisible the moment it is named, because the scope filter reads a scope derived from the launch agent and main has no manifest to be launched with. Pinned on the named-call returning zero rather than on the member id, so a fix that lets main through drifts this entry while a fix that merely renames the fixture's session does not. The unfiltered call is the case's own control: if it stopped seeing the membership, the finding would be a fixture artifact and reports as malformed instead.

The pin is the count so closing any part of the property drifts this entry rather than shrinking it quietly. Session-end extract computes scan_for_secrets and binds it to `_`; ingest archives fetched bytes without scanning at all; retain_ingress_receipt archives a Cursor session's ingress evidence and never scans it. Not a claim that the scanner is wrong (it flags the canary) or that redaction is owed — docs/10 chose report-never-redact on purpose. The claim is that the report has no reader on any path that runs. Re-pinned from '2 site(s)': the defect widened rather than closed. 7c1107e added retain_ingress_receipt and 13f4530 its call site, opening a third unscanned archive path. A second consumer of the findings existed for one day (ccff774 printed them in `_cmd_arch`, 0fef9b6 removed that block); the only surviving consumer is bootstrap.py:150, which is the same one that existed at the original triage.

The claim is narrow and it is the claim being pinned: a dial stamped into ranker_fingerprint as the configuration in force is captured where rebinding cannot reach it. Not a claim that the shipped value 8 is wrong. This shape has already produced a published wrong number once (lab/030 measured the cap as having zero effect because patching the constant did nothing while the run labelled itself with the patched value). Pinned on the capture site rather than the line number, which unrelated edits would move; a second dial acquiring a capture changes the witness and drifts this entry.
